      "content":"# 231 — Move per-language signature parsers out of the file browser into `langs/<name>/parser.js`\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\n`assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` carries language-specific code:\n- `parse_lua(content)` — extracts `function M.<name>(<params>)`\n  declarations and scans for `return` statements to enumerate\n  outputs.\n- `parse_bash(content)` — extracts `<name>() {` declarations and\n  uses `parse_bash_inputs` to count `$N` references.\n- `parse_functions(content, filename)` — dispatches on file\n  extension to one of the above.\n\nC has no parser yet. Languages a user might add (Python, Rust, …)\nhave no path to a parser.\n\nThe lexer infrastructure (issue 223, complete) already establishes\nthe right pattern: per-language files under `langs/<name>/`,\nloaded on demand by the editor through dynamic `import()`. The\nsignature parsers belong there, not in the editor.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEach language directory carries a `parser.js` ES module exporting\na single function:\n\n```js\n// langs/<name>/parser.js\nexport function parse_functions(content) {\n  return [\n    {\n      name: 'write_result',\n      inputs: ['text'],\n      outputs: [],            // empty array → sink box (issue 226)\n      variadic_base: null,    // or 'args' for f(a, ...)\n    },\n    // ...\n  ];\n}\n```\n\nThe editor's file browser drops its `parse_lua` / `parse_bash` /\n`parse_functions` and asks the per-language parser instead. Same\nlazy-load pattern as the lexers: a registry keyed by file\nextension, dynamic `import()` on first need, cached per session.\nFiles with an unknown extension fall back to \"no parser available\"\n— the file browser displays the file name but offers no\nfunction-list step.\n\n### Extended return shape\n\nThe parser returns a richer record than the current shape:\n- `name` — function name (existing).\n- `inputs` — array of parameter names in declaration order\n  (existing).\n- `outputs` — array of return-value names; empty for sinks\n  (existing).\n- `variadic_base` — string or null. Set when the function\n  declaration has a variadic tail (Lua `...`, Bash `\"$@\"`, C\n  `va_list`). Editor uses it to auto-flip the var toggle for that\n  port. Existing parsers don't compute this; new field, optional\n  for parsers that don't bother.\n\n### Why this matters\n\nThe file browser is the editor's single entry point for \"import\nfunction from source.\" Any language-specific logic in it is the\nwrong level of abstraction. Moving it puts the editor on equal\nfooting with the runtime: both treat languages as pluggable, both\ndiscover capabilities through `langs/<name>/`, neither has a\nhardcoded list.\n\nIt also makes adding a new language a self-contained job: drop\n`langs/<name>/parser.js`, `langs/<name>/lexer.js`, and (phase 3)\n`langs/<name>/spec.so` into `langs/`, and the editor and the\nrunner both pick it up.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Create `langs/lua/parser.js` with the existing `parse_lua` /\n   `parse_lua_returns` logic, exporting `parse_functions`.\n2. Create `langs/bash/parser.js` with the existing `parse_bash` /\n   `parse_bash_inputs` logic.\n3. Optionally create `langs/c/parser.js` — a minimal one that\n   extracts `int name(int a, char *b)` style declarations from\n   header files. Defer if not needed yet.\n4. Add a parser registry to `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` mirroring\n   the lexer registry in `008-source-view.js`:\n   ```js\n   const EXT_TO_LANG = { lua: 'lua', sh: 'bash', bash: 'bash' };\n   const parser_cache = {};\n   async function load_parser(lang) { /* dynamic import */ }\n   ```\n5. Replace `parse_functions(content, filename)` body with a lookup\n   into the registry. The function becomes async; existing callers\n   already `await` async file fetches, so this slots in.\n6. Delete `parse_lua`, `parse_bash`, `parse_lua_returns`,\n   `parse_bash_inputs`, `lua_fn_end` from `007-filebrowser.js`.\n7. (Optional, separate change) Wire `variadic_base` into the\n   on-select handler so the editor auto-flips the var toggle.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Test coverage**: parsers are easy to break with a regex tweak.\n  A small set of fixture sources (`maps/_test/parser-fixtures/*.lua`,\n  `*.sh`) and a JS test harness would catch regressions.     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: ```json
{
  "userType":"external",
  "parentUuid":"106485c3-6a2b-4ba2-8f67-e02e0a7f1cbe",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-20T02:46:13.334Z",
  "isSidechain":false,

  "toolUseResult":{
    "newString":"# 231 — Move per-language signature parsers out of the file browser into `langs/<name>/parser.js`\n\n## Status\ncomplete (2026-05-19) — lua + bash parsers and their editor-facing\nlanguage specs moved into `langs/<lang>/`, file browser is now\nlanguage-agnostic. C parser explicitly deferred per the original\nstep 3. Test coverage lands under issue 232.",
    "userModified":false,
    "oldString":"# 231 — Move per-language signature parsers out of the file browser into `langs/<name>/parser.js`\n\n## Status\nopen",
    "structuredPatch":[{
        "oldStart":1,
        "oldLines":7,
        "newStart":1,
        "newLines":10,
        "lines":[" # 231 — Move per-language signature parsers out of the file browser into `langs/<name>/parser.js`"," "," ## Status","-open","+complete (2026-05-19) — lua + bash parsers and their editor-facing","+language specs moved into `langs/<lang>/`, file browser is now","+language-agnostic. C parser explicitly deferred per the original","+step 3. Test coverage lands under issue 232."," "," ## Current behavior"," "]
      }],
    "replaceAll":false,
    "originalFile":"# 231 — Move per-language signature parsers out of the file browser into `langs/<name>/parser.js`\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\n`assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` carries language-specific code:\n- `parse_lua(content)` — extracts `function M.<name>(<params>)`\n  declarations and scans for `return` statements to enumerate\n  outputs.\n- `parse_bash(content)` — extracts `<name>() {` declarations and\n  uses `parse_bash_inputs` to count `$N` references.\n- `parse_functions(content, filename)` — dispatches on file\n  extension to one of the above.\n\nC has no parser yet. Languages a user might add (Python, Rust, …)\nhave no path to a parser.\n\nThe lexer infrastructure (issue 223, complete) already establishes\nthe right pattern: per-language files under `langs/<name>/`,\nloaded on demand by the editor through dynamic `import()`. The\nsignature parsers belong there, not in the editor.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEach language directory carries a `parser.js` ES module exporting\na single function:\n\n```js\n// langs/<name>/parser.js\nexport function parse_functions(content) {\n  return [\n    {\n      name: 'write_result',\n      inputs: ['text'],\n      outputs: [],            // empty array → sink box (issue 226)\n      variadic_base: null,    // or 'args' for f(a, ...)\n    },\n    // ...\n  ];\n}\n```\n\nThe editor's file browser drops its `parse_lua` / `parse_bash` /\n`parse_functions` and asks the per-language parser instead. Same\nlazy-load pattern as the lexers: a registry keyed by file\nextension, dynamic `import()` on first need, cached per session.\nFiles with an unknown extension fall back to \"no parser available\"\n— the file browser displays the file name but offers no\nfunction-list step.\n\n### Extended return shape\n\nThe parser returns a richer record than the current shape:\n- `name` — function name (existing).\n- `inputs` — array of parameter names in declaration order\n  (existing).\n- `outputs` — array of return-value names; empty for sinks\n  (existing).\n- `variadic_base` — string or null. Set when the function\n  declaration has a variadic tail (Lua `...`, Bash `\"$@\"`, C\n  `va_list`). Editor uses it to auto-flip the var toggle for that\n  port. Existing parsers don't compute this; new field, optional\n  for parsers that don't bother.\n\n### Why this matters\n\nThe file browser is the editor's single entry point for \"import\nfunction from source.\" Any language-specific logic in it is the\nwrong level of abstraction. Moving it puts the editor on equal\nfooting with the runtime: both treat languages as pluggable, both\ndiscover capabilities through `langs/<name>/`, neither has a\nhardcoded list.\n\nIt also makes adding a new language a self-contained job: drop\n`langs/<name>/parser.js`, `langs/<name>/lexer.js`, and (phase 3)\n`langs/<name>/spec.so` into `langs/`, and the editor and the\nrunner both pick it up.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Create `langs/lua/parser.js` with the existing `parse_lua` /\n   `parse_lua_returns` logic, exporting `parse_functions`.\n2. Create `langs/bash/parser.js` with the existing `parse_bash` /\n   `parse_bash_inputs` logic.\n3. Optionally create `langs/c/parser.js` — a minimal one that\n   extracts `int name(int a, char *b)` style declarations from\n   header files. Defer if not needed yet.\n4. Add a parser registry to `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` mirroring\n   the lexer registry in `008-source-view.js`:\n   ```js\n   const EXT_TO_LANG = { lua: 'lua', sh: 'bash', bash: 'bash' };\n   const parser_cache = {};\n   async function load_parser(lang) { /* dynamic import */ }\n   ```\n5. Replace `parse_functions(content, filename)` body with a lookup\n   into the registry. The function becomes async; existing callers\n   already `await` async file fetches, so this slots in.\n6. Delete `parse_lua`, `parse_bash`, `parse_lua_returns`,\n   `parse_bash_inputs`, `lua_fn_end` from `007-filebrowser.js`.\n7. (Optional, separate change) Wire `variadic_base` into the\n   on-select handler so the editor auto-flips the var toggle.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Test coverage**: parsers are easy to break with a regex tweak.\n  A small set of fixture sources (`maps/_test/parser-fixtures/*.lua`,\n  `*.sh`) and a JS test harness would catch regressions. Out of\n  scope for this issue, worth a follow-up.\n- **Parsing failure shape**: a parser that throws should be\n  reported as \"parser error\" not \"no parser.\" Add a try/catch in\n  the registry layer with a clear message.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — current parsers move out\n- `langs/lua/parser.js` — new\n- `langs/bash/parser.js` — new\n- `langs/lua/lexer.js`, `langs/bash/lexer.js` — peer modules; same\n  loading pattern\n- `assets/js/008-source-view.js` — reference implementation for\n  the lazy lexer registry\n- `issues/completed/223-syntax-highlighting-via-user-lexers.md` —\n  established the `langs/<name>/<file>` server-serve route and the\n  dynamic-import loading model\n- `docs/005-language-specs.md` — add a \"parser interface\" section\n  alongside the existing \"lexer interface\"\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/231-move-signature-parsers-into-langs.md"
  },

As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. The slot store, the\nlarge-value heap, anything else that holds wire values — they all\nend up funneled through the same pool. Eager neighbor-merge on\nreturn keeps fragmentation honest for the common case; a deeper\nsweep runs on demand when an allocation would otherwise have to\ngrow the region. Pre-warmed free-lists handle the static class\nsizes a map declares at compile time; growth is the rare last\nresort. Thread-safe via per-class mutexes — different sizes never\ncontend.\n\nThis is the standalone module. Wiring it into the slot store is the\nnext slice of issue 302.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",

    "replaceAll":false,
    "originalFile":"/* tests/317-lua-bridge-test.c — Lua spec native↔JSON bridges.\n *\n * Loads langs/lua/spec.so through the spec registry and exercises\n * `native_to_json` and `json_to_native` together. The strategy is a\n * round-trip: feed a JSON string in via `json_to_native` (which\n * pushes a Lua value on the worker's lua_State), then yank it back\n * out via `native_to_json` (which reads top-of-stack and writes JSON\n * to a buffer). If the input and output match, both halves of the\n * bridge agree on the encoding.\n *\n * The round-trip approach keeps this test free of any direct\n * dependency on the LuaJIT headers — the bridges are the only thing\n * the test calls, and the lua_State is opaque from C's side. That\n * matches the cross-language wire-format design (issue 317): callers\n * never need to know Lua's internals to move data through it.\n *\n * Run from the project root so the spec dlopen path resolves.\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ load_lua_spec() — boot the registry and find the lua spec */\nstatic const lang_spec_t *load_lua_spec(spec_registry_t **out_reg)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!r) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"registry load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    const lang_spec_t *lua = spec_registry_get(r, \"lua\");\n    if (!lua || !lua->init || !lua->teardown\n            || !lua->native_to_json || !lua->json_to_native) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec missing bridge callbacks\\n\");\n        spec_registry_destroy(r);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    *out_reg = r;\n    return lua;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ roundtrip() — JSON → Lua stack → JSON, compare to expected */\n/* Convenience used by every test case. `expected` is the canonical\n * JSON the bridge should emit on the way back; if NULL, the input\n * itself is the expected output. Returns 1 on success. */\nstatic int roundtrip(const lang_spec_t *lua, void *h,\n                     const char *input, const char *expected)\n{\n    char out[512];\n    int  out_size = 0;\n    int  rc = lua->json_to_native(h, input, (int)strlen(input),\n                                  NULL, 0, NULL);\n    if (rc != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      json_to_native failed for '%s'\\n\", input);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    rc = lua->native_to_json(h, NULL, 0, out, (int)sizeof(out), &out_size);\n    if (rc != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      native_to_json failed for '%s'\\n\", input);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    out[out_size] = '\\0';\n    const char *want = expected ? expected : input;\n    if (strcmp(out, want) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      mismatch: want '%s', got '%s'\\n\", want, out);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_scalars() — null, bool, integer, float, string */\nstatic int test_scalars(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *lua = load_lua_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(lua);\n    void *h = lua->init(0);\n    ASSERT(h);\n\n    /* Integer-shaped Lua numbers round-trip as integers (3, not 3.0)\n     * because encode_value picks the int writer for whole values.\n     * \"null\" round-trips because nil → null → nil. */\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"null\",      NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"true\",      NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"false\",     NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"0\",         NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"42\",        NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"-17\",       NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"\\\"\\\"\",      NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"\\\"hello\\\"\", NULL));\n\n    lua->teardown(h);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_arrays() — sequence tables round-trip as JSON arrays */\nstatic int test_arrays(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *lua = load_lua_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(lua);\n    void *h = lua->init(0);\n\n    /* Empty array is the one shape we *can't* round-trip as []\n     * because an empty Lua table can't be told apart from {} on the\n     * way out (see encode_value's array-vs-object heuristic). The\n     * round-trip canonicalises [] to {} — a deliberate, documented\n     * choice. Every non-empty sequence works as expected. */\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"[]\",                \"{}\"));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"[1]\",               NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"[1,2,3]\",           NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"[\\\"a\\\",\\\"b\\\"]\",     NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"[[1,2],[3,4]]\",     NULL));\n\n    /* Lua impedance: `null` inside an array becomes `nil`, which\n     * truncates the table's # length at the first hole. JSON's\n     * \"trailing nulls are still slots\" semantics has no native Lua\n     * shape. We document this by asserting the truncation rather\n     * than pretending it round-trips. A future $lang_opaque or\n     * an explicit n-field convention is the way out, but not\n     * today. */\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"[true,false,null]\", \"[true,false]\"));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"[1,2,null]\",        \"[1,2]\"));\n\n    lua->teardown(h);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_objects() — keyed tables round-trip as JSON objects */\n/* Object key ordering inside a Lua table is not guaranteed to\n * match the input — Lua's table iteration order is implementation\n * defined. We test single-key objects (no ordering ambiguity) and\n * nested structure for the multi-key case. */\nstatic int test_objects(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *lua = load_lua_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(lua);\n    void *h = lua->init(0);\n\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"{}\",            NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"{\\\"x\\\":1}\",     NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"{\\\"a\\\":\\\"b\\\"}\", NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"{\\\"nest\\\":{\\\"k\\\":42}}\", NULL));\n    ASSERT(roundtrip(lua, h, \"{\\\"items\\\":[1,2,3]}\",   NULL));\n\n    lua->teardown(h);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_truncation() — undersized buffer is a loud error */\n/* Project convention forbids silent fallbacks. A too-small output\n * buffer must surface as a nonzero return from native_to_json,\n * not a truncated-but-success path. */\nstatic int test_truncation(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *lua = load_lua_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(lua);\n    void *h = lua->init(0);\n\n    int rc = lua->json_to_native(h, \"[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9]\",\n                                 (int)strlen(\"[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9]\"),\n                                 NULL, 0, NULL);\n    ASSERT(rc == 0);\n\n    char tiny[4];\n    int  out_size = 0;\n    rc = lua->native_to_json(h, NULL, 0, tiny, (int)sizeof(tiny), &out_size);\n    ASSERT(rc != 0);\n\n    lua->teardown(h);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_parse_error() — malformed JSON returns nonzero */\nstatic int test_parse_error(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *lua = load_lua_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(lua);\n    void *h = lua->init(0);\n\n    int rc = lua->json_to_native(h, \"{not json\", 9, NULL, 0, NULL);\n    ASSERT(rc != 0);\n\n    lua->teardown(h);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs/lua/spec.so\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"317-lua-bridge-test: langs/lua/spec.so not built; \"\n                        \"run `make specs` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"317-lua-bridge-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(scalars);\n    RUN(arrays);\n    RUN(objects);\n    RUN(truncation);\n    RUN(parse_error);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/317-lua-bridge-test.c"
  },
  "slug":"ancient-bouncing-wall",
  "sessionId":"e9ed70c7-2b63-425c-987c-6431040bedfb",

        },
        "type":"tool_use",
        "input":{
          "new_string":"### 2026-05-19 — stage 2: Lua array fidelity\n\nStage 1 lost `null` inside arrays — `[true,false,null]` round-tripped\nas `[true,false]`. Stage 2 fixes it by applying the n-field\nconvention from the fidelity directive below.\n\nWhat changed in the code:\n\n- `decode_node` (JSON → Lua): the JSON_ARRAY case now creates a Lua\n  table with a string key `n` set to the array's length, then\n  fills integer keys 1..n. JSON `null` elements use `lua_rawseti`\n  with nil — which deletes the key, leaving an absent slot. The\n  table now carries enough information to reconstruct the array\n  losslessly.\n\n- `encode_value` (Lua → JSON): table emission reads `n` first. If\n  the field is a non-negative integer, the table is treated as a\n  declared-length array — the encoder walks 1..n and emits null\n  for any missing slot via the existing nil → null path. Tables\n  without `n` fall through to the existing array-vs-object\n  heuristic for idiomatic Lua values.\n\nWhat the tests prove now:\n\n- `[]`, `[null]`, `[null,null]`, `[null,1,2]`, `[1,null,3]`,\n  `[1,2,null]`, `[true,false,null]` all round-trip exactly.\n\nWhat this costs:\n\n- Lua tables that have crossed the bridge carry a `n` field\n  visible to `pairs()`. The fidelity directive accepts this:\n  \"We can intrude on idiomatic Lua because we're fundamentally\n  translating from Lua to JSON.\" Box authors who write Lua\n  tables by hand and want them treated as JSON arrays can also\n  set `n` themselves; otherwise the existing heuristic still\n  catches `{1, 2, 3}`-shaped tables.",
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"**Known impedance-mismatch case (documented in the test):** `null`\ninside a JSON array becomes Lua `nil`, and `lua_objlen` truncates\nthe sequence at the first hole. The bridge round-trips\n`[true,false,null]` as `[true,false]`. This is fundamental Lua\nsemantics and is asserted explicitly rather than glossed over.\n\nThis stage-1 lossiness is **not the final design.** See the\nfidelity directive below — stage 2 must preserve the JSON shape\nthrough Lua via an explicit length field, accepting that this\nintrudes on idiomatic Lua.",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/317-spec-json-bridge-for-data-boxes.md"
        }
      }],

          "command":"git add langs/lua/spec.c tests/317-lua-bridge-test.c issues/317-spec-json-bridge-for-data-boxes.md && git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n317 stage 2 — Lua arrays preserve every JSON shape\n\nStage 1 of the Lua ↔ JSON bridge silently lost `null` inside\narrays. Lua's tables can't store nil in a slot, so `[true,false,null]`\ncame back as `[true,false]` — a faithful Lua representation, but a\nbroken cross-language wire. The fidelity directive in 317 forbids\nsilent loss: the wire must carry every shape JSON expresses, and\nthe bridge intrudes on the host language as needed to do it.\n\nThe fix: the decoder records the intended length of every array\non the Lua side as a small `n` field, and the encoder reads it\nback to walk a full-length array, emitting null at every absent\nslot. Idiomatic Lua values without an `n` field still take the\nexisting array-vs-object heuristic. Box authors who want to hand-\nwrite a Lua table that becomes a JSON array with embedded nulls\ncan do so by setting `n` themselves.\n\nEmbedded, leading, trailing, and all-null arrays all round-trip\nexactly now. The cost is a visible `n` key on tables that have\ncrossed the bridge — the directive accepts this trade.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Commit stage 2"
        }
      }],

{
  "userType":"external",

        "type":"text",
        "text":"Stage 2 in. Summary:\n\n- **Encoder** reads `n` first; if non-negative integer, emits a fixed-length array (`json_writer_null` for missing slots through the existing nil path).\n- **Decoder** sets `t.n = len` and uses `lua_rawseti` with nil to leave deletion-of-key (no key) for null elements.\n- **Tests**: 5/5, including the new `[null]`, `[null,1,2]`, `[1,null,3]`, `[null,null]`, `[true,false,null]` cases that stage 1 truncated.\n- **Trade documented**: a Lua table that came through the bridge carries a visible `n` key — the fidelity directive accepted this.\n\nFull suite green. Commit `82690ad`.\n\nWorking tree is back to just the held `229` doc. Where next? Options on the table:\n\n1. **317 next slice — type-tag wrapper for ambiguity** (e.g. int vs float when Lua's whole-number `2` should reach a C `float` slot as `2.0`). Pairs with the C bridge work below.\n2. **Bash bridge** — near-identity, smallest of the three, gets us one step closer to data boxes working end-to-end. No `handle` needed since bash scripts already deal in text.\n3. **C bridge** — depends on 307's typed wrapper. Scalar-only first cut still useful.\n4. **Wire the bridges into dispatch** (issue 312's classification path) so cross-language edges actually call them. Without this step the bridges are dead code on the wire.\n5. **229** — now that 317 stage 2 is in, your \"read/write box-kinds\" design has a working JSON bridge to assume.\n\nI'd suggest **4** — bridges are useless until dispatch calls them, and even the Lua-Lua case benefits from the round-trip going through them in the cross-language-edge case. What's your call?"

      "content":"# 229 — `read` and `write` box kinds (language-aware file IO)\n\n## Status\nopen (redesigned 2026-05-19 — supersedes the earlier \"data source +\nfile_write sink\" and the still-earlier \"data kind / literal-or-file\nunified source\" proposals, both kept below for history)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe `data` kind is recognized by the schema and accepted by the\nloader, but has no runtime semantics distinct from `call`. It\ncarries `ref` and `fn` like a call box and runs through whichever\nlanguage driver matches the file extension. The green badge on\nthe canvas is purely cosmetic — the box behaves exactly like\n`call`.\n\n`libs/files.lua::read_text` and friends cover the actual \"read a\ntext file\" case (issue 216, complete) via regular call boxes,\nbut only from Lua. A Bash function that needs file contents has\nto wire through a Lua read box, which is a language-coupling no\ngraph reader expects.\n\n## Intended behavior — two kinds, `read` and `write`\n\nBoth are dispatch-layer primitives — no language driver runs for\ntheir core IO. The language specs DO participate at the wire\nboundary so the value crosses cross-language seams natively (see\n\"language-aware IO\" below). The phase-3 entry point lives in\n`src/012-dispatch.c`; the phase-2 mirror lives in\n`src/004-executor.lua` so the editor's \"test run\" works the same.\n\n### `read` — emits a value\n\nA `read` box has one input port and one output port. The output\nis **always trusted to produce a value** — that's the box's\nsingle job, and downstream consumers can rely on it.\n\n| port | direction | type   | meaning                            |\n|------|-----------|--------|-------------------------------------|\n| path | in        | string | path to the file on disk            |\n| (single output) | out | any | the value to emit                 |\n\nNo `ref`, no `fn`. The box decides what to emit using this\nprecedence:\n\n1. If the inspector carries an **inline literal value** for the\n   box, emit that directly. **The `path` input port hides on the\n   canvas** in this mode — there's no file involved, and a path\n   port on a box that doesn't read a file would just confuse the\n   reader.\n2. Else if `path` is supplied (via wire or via an inline literal\n   path on the input port), read that file from disk and emit its\n   contents.\n3. Else error — a `read` with neither a literal nor a path is a\n   misconfiguration the validator should catch.\n\n### `write` — emits a done signal\n\n| port  | direction | type   | meaning                            |\n|-------|-----------|--------|-------------------------------------|\n| path  | in        | string | destination path                    |\n| value | in        | any    | the content to write                |\n| (single output) | out | boolean | `true` when the write completed |\n\nThe output is intentionally minimal — a boolean done signal\nthat downstream graphs can fan into \"and now the file is on\ndisk, fire the next thing\" patterns. It's also easy to ignore\nwhen no one cares: per the unwired-output discard rule\n(documented when this issue lands), a `write` with no wire on\nits output produces the boolean and drops it.\n\nAtomic write: write to `path.tmp`, fsync, rename to `path`.\nSame convention `soramech-data` already uses.\n\n### Canvas colors\n\n- `read` keeps the existing green for data boxes (`#4caf7d`) so\n  source-of-truth-for-a-value boxes read consistently from old\n  maps that still call them `data`.\n- `write` gets **orange cheddar — `#d4762a`** (vivid, dark side,\n  warm). The contrast against `read`'s green makes source vs\n  sink visually obvious at a glance.\n\n### Why two kinds and not one unified `data` box\n\nA previous revision of this issue proposed a single `data` kind\nthat could be source, sink, or constant depending on its\nconfiguration. That collapsed to ambiguity:\n\n- Two ways to source the output (literal vs file) needed a\n  precedence rule.\n- Read and write both want `path` — a \"wrote without meaning to\"\n  footgun lurks when the user forgets to wire `value`.\n- The output port carries fundamentally different semantics by\n  mode (file contents vs done signal vs literal).\n- A canvas reader can't tell what the box does from its shape.\n\nSource vs sink IS the natural seam. `read` always emits a value\n(literal or file). `write` always commits a value to disk.\nDifferent action, different identity, different color.\n\n## Language-aware IO (depends on issue 317)\n\nEvery cross-language seam in the graph goes through the\n`native_to_json` / `json_to_native` callbacks issue 317 adds to\neach `lang_spec_t`. `read` and `write` use that same machinery\nso a Lua data file feeding a C consumer arrives as a native C\nvalue, and a C struct flowing into a `write` is serialized via\nthe C spec rather than blindly stringified by the dispatch\nlayer.\n\n### `read` per-downstream-wire fan-out\n\nA `read` box's single output port can have **N downstream\nwires**, each ending at a box in possibly different languages.\nThe dispatch layer:\n\n1. Sources the value (literal or file bytes).\n2. Iterates the box's outgoing wires. For each:\n   a. Looks up the target box's language via its `ref` extension\n      (or the routing layer's pre-classified `lang` from issue 305).\n   b. Calls that language's `json_to_native` to lift the value\n      into the target language's native form.\n   c. Hands the native value to the target box's input slot.\n\nIf three wires go to a C box, a Lua box, and a Bash box, the\ndispatch loop runs the conversion three times — once per spec.\n**Downstream boxes treat the `read` box's output as native to\ntheir own language.** No SoraMech-specific glue at the consumer.\n\nFor files on disk, `read` treats the file contents as JSON text —\nthe canonical wire format — and feeds those bytes to each\ndownstream spec's `json_to_native`. A Lua user writing a file by\nhand still writes JSON (or uses a `write` box upstream, which\nproduces JSON anyway).\n\n### `write` per-upstream-wire dispatch\n\nA `write` box's `value` input is fed by exactly one upstream\nwire. The dispatch layer:\n\n1. Looks up the source box's language.\n2. Calls that language's `native_to_json` to canonicalize the\n   value to JSON text.\n3. Writes the JSON bytes to `path` atomically.\n\nIf the source is a Lua box returning a table, the Lua spec\nencodes the table to JSON. If the source is a C box returning a\nstruct, the C spec walks the type. The user never sees the\nserialization step — it's the spec's job, not the box author's.\n\n### Why this matters\n\nThe user's mental model is \"I write code in my language, the\ndata crosses the wire, the other side gets it in their\nlanguage.\" `read` and `write` should reinforce that, not break\nit. Either box would otherwise be the place where the user is\nforced to think about JSON shapes, byte order, or string\nescapes. With the spec-driven IO callbacks, all of that lives\nwhere it belongs — in the language specs.\n\n### Dependency relationship with 317\n\n229 cannot land cleanly without 317. The cross-language emit/write\nbehavior described above IS 317's contract; this issue just names\nthe runtime primitives that make first use of it. Implementation\norder: 317 → 229. If 229 lands first with a stub \"everything goes\nthrough bash-style text identity,\" the result is plain string IO\nwith no Lua-table / C-struct support, which is a regression from\nthe design goal.\n\n## Schema\n\n**read** (default file-source form):\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"load_cfg\",\n  \"kind\": \"read\",\n  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"path\" }],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 100 }\n}\n```\n\n**read** with inline literal value (no path port):\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"default_prompt\",\n  \"kind\": \"read\",\n  \"value\": \"You are a helpful assistant.\",\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 100 }\n}\n```\n\n**read** with inline literal path (path port still present\non canvas if no `value` is set, but the port's label shows\nthe literal — same convention as issue 235):\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"load_cfg\",\n  \"kind\": \"read\",\n  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"path\", \"value\": \"config.json\" }],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 100 }\n}\n```\n\n**write**:\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"save_result\",\n  \"kind\": \"write\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"path\" },\n    { \"name\": \"value\" }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 400, \"y\": 100 }\n}\n```\n\n## Inspector behavior\n\n### `read`\n\n- **Inline value** field (textarea / text input): a free-form\n  literal that, when non-empty, becomes the box's output and\n  HIDES the `path` input port on the canvas. Same hide-when-\n  literal precedence is the obvious progression of issue 235's\n  \"literal value replaces port name\" idea, applied to the port\n  itself.\n- **Path** field: the literal-on-port equivalent for the `path`\n  input. Disabled when the inline value is set.\n- The two fields are mutually-illuminating: typing into one\n  visibly disables the other so the user always knows which\n  mode the box is in.\n\n### `write`\n\n- Two input port rows (`path`, `value`) with the standard\n  port literal / wire UI.\n- No inline-value field (a `write` with no value to commit\n  is meaningless).\n\n### Kind dropdown\n\nReplace the current `['call', 'data']` list with\n`['call', 'read', 'write']`. Picking a kind from this dropdown\nswaps the box's input/output shape per the schemas above.\n\n## Migration\n\nLegacy `data` boxes (the cosmetic-only kind) get rewritten by\nthe loader. Two paths:\n\n- Boxes with a `ref` / `fn` (the call-equivalent shape they\n  carry today) → rewrite `kind` to `call`. Behavior identical\n  to current.\n- Boxes without a `ref` / `fn` (rare — would be invalid today)\n  → rewrite to `read` with no path; the validator then flags\n  them so the user notices and fills in a path or literal.\n\nThe `data` kind is retired entirely. The schema rejects it\nafter migration runs once.\n\n## Unwired-output discard rule\n\nThe general rule this issue makes use of, applicable to every\nbox:\n\n> **If an output value is produced but no wire carries it\n> downstream, the value is discarded.**\n\nA `write` box's done boolean is the most visible case — a user\nwho doesn't need a chain-after-write trigger leaves the output\nunwired and the runtime drops the value. The rule already holds\ninformally for every box; documenting it here (and in\n`docs/001-architecture.md`) makes it explicit.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. **Block on 317**: cross-language emit/write callbacks must be\n   in place. Without them this issue degrades to plain-text IO.\n2. **Schema** (`src/001-schema.lua`, `src/010-graph-loader.c`):\n   accept `read` and `write`; retire `data`.\n3. **Loader migration** (`src/003-loader.lua`): rewrite legacy\n   `data` boxes per the migration section.\n4. **Phase 2 executor** (`src/004-executor.lua`): handle `read`\n   (literal or file) and `write` directly. Cross-language\n   conversion uses the spec callbacks via the same path as\n   call-box value transport.\n5. **Phase 3 dispatch** (`src/012-dispatch.c`): same handling at\n   the dispatch layer. `read`'s fan-out loops through downstream\n   wires per spec; `write` looks up source-spec on its `value`\n   input.\n6. **Inspector** (`assets/js/004-inspector.js`): kind-specific\n   layout per \"Inspector behavior\" above. The inline-value field\n   for `read` is new; the port-hide-when-literal-value behavior\n   is new and needs a small render-side hook in `draw_box`.\n7. **Box rendering** (`assets/js/002-boxes.js`):\n   - Add `read: '#4caf7d'` and `write: '#d4762a'` to `KIND_COLOR`.\n   - Add `read`/`write` to the `KIND_HEADER` map from issue 236.\n   - Honor `hide_port` flag (or equivalent) on the path input\n     when the inline value is set on a `read` box.\n8. **Documentation**: update `docs/001-architecture.md` with the\n   new kinds, the unwired-output rule, and the language-aware\n   IO behavior. Update the dispatch-layer info.md.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Output port labels** for `read` and `write`: `contents` for\n  read, `done` for write — pick once, document, move on. Issue\n  236 already established the per-kind output-label table; add\n  these two rows.\n- **Static path on `write`**: should `write` also accept an\n  inline literal path on its `path` port (same way `read`\n  does)? Probably yes — the use case \"save to a fixed location\n  every time\" is common. Comes free if we apply the existing\n  port-literal-value mechanism.\n- **`read` with both literal and path set on disk** (a user who\n  edits the JSON by hand and sets both): validator rejects, or\n  literal-wins? Validator rejects — explicit error rather than\n  hidden precedence.\n- **Cross-language type fidelity** for the C spec: walking\n  arbitrary C structs is rabbit-hole territory (issue 317\n  tracks this). Until C's `native_to_json` handles structs,\n  C-source `write` boxes are limited to scalar values. Same\n  limitation issue 317 documents.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — kind validation, new shapes\n- `src/010-graph-loader.c` — C-side schema, migration\n- `src/003-loader.lua` — legacy `data` rewrite\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — phase 2 runtime handling\n- `src/012-dispatch.c` — phase 3 dispatch primitives\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — kind-specific inspector layout\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — color, header, port-hide on literal\n- `langs/{lua,c,bash}/spec.c` — `native_to_json` / `json_to_native`\n  (issue 317 owns these)\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — kinds section, unwired-output rule\n- `issues/317-spec-json-bridge-for-data-boxes.md` — hard dependency\n- `issues/235-...completed/` — literal-replaces-port-name idea\n  extended to \"literal hides port entirely\" here\n- `issues/236-...completed/` — per-kind header/output-label map\n- `issues/completed/216-read-file-box.md` — Lua-side read superseded\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — phase 3 home for these\n- `issues/completed/109-data-files-persistent-and-ephemeral.md` —\n  `soramech-data` is a separate concern; not affected\n\n---\n\n## Historical proposals (superseded)\n\n### Revision 2 (single `data` kind, literal-or-file)\n\nProposed one unified source box: literal value typed in the\ninspector OR file at `path`. Plus a separate `write` sink.\nRejected because the source-and-sink-in-one-kind ambiguity\nanalysis (above, in \"Why two kinds\") flagged real footguns —\nthe `path`-input-without-`value` case silently reading from\na file the user meant to write to.\n\n### Revision 1 (`data` source + `file_write` sink)\n\nProposed a `data` kind (no inputs, just a `path` field; emits\nfile bytes) and a separate write-sink. Renamed in revision 2\nto `read` / `write` because verbs match what the boxes do\nbetter than `data` does. Both revisions kept the same source\n/ sink split.\n\nThe binary-data, atomic-write, JSON-parsing, and dispatch-layer\nhome questions all carry over unchanged through every\nrevision.\n",

If 229 lands first with a stub \"everything goes\n168\tthrough bash-style text identity,\" the result is plain string IO\n169\twith no Lua-table / C-struct support, which is a regression from\n170\tthe design goal.\n171\t\n172\t## Schema\n173\t\n174\t**read** (default file-source form):\n175\t```json\n176\t{\n177\t  \"id\": \"load_cfg\",\n178\t  \"kind\": \"read\",\n179\t  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"path\" }],\n180\t  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 100 }\n181\t}\n182\t```\n183\t\n184\t**read** with inline literal value (no path port):\n185\t```json\n186\t{\n187\t  \"id\": \"default_prompt\",\n188\t  \"kind\": \"read\",\n189\t  \"value\": \"You are a helpful assistant.\",\n190\t  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 100 }\n191\t}\n192\t```\n193\t\n194\t**read** with inline literal path (path port still present\n195\ton canvas if no `value` is set, but the port's label shows\n196\tthe literal — same convention as issue 235):\n197\t```json\n198\t{\n199\t  \"id\": \"load_cfg\",\n200\t  \"kind\": \"read\",\n201\t  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"path\", \"value\": \"config.json\" }],\n202\t  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 100 }\n203\t}\n204\t```\n205\t\n206\t**write**:\n207\t```json\n208\t{\n209\t  \"id\": \"save_result\",\n210\t  \"kind\": \"write\",\n211\t  \"inputs\": [\n212\t    { \"name\": \"path\" },\n213\t    { \"name\": \"value\" }\n214\t  ],\n215\t  \"ui\": { \"x\": 400, \"y\": 100 }\n216\t}\n217\t```\n218\t\n219\t## Inspector behavior\n220\t\n221\t### `read`\n222\t\n223\t- **Inline value** field (textarea / text input): a free-form\n224\t  literal that, when non-empty, becomes the box's output and\n225\t  HIDES the `path` input port on the canvas. Same hide-when-\n226\t  literal precedence is the obvious progression of issue 235's\n227\t  \"literal value replaces port name\" idea, applied to the port\n228\t  itself.\n229\t- **Path** field: the literal-on-port equivalent for the `path`\n230\t  input. Disabled when the inline value is set.\n231\t- The two fields are mutually-illuminating: typing into one\n232\t  visibly disables the other so the user always knows which\n233\t  mode the box is in.\n234\t\n235\t### `write`\n236\t\n237\t- Two input port rows (`path`, `value`) with the standard\n238\t  port literal / wire UI.\n239\t- No inline-value field (a `write` with no value to commit\n240\t  is meaningless).\n241\t\n242\t### Kind dropdown\n243\t\n244\tReplace the current `['call', 'data']` list with\n245\t`['call', 'read', 'write']`. Picking a kind from this dropdown\n246\tswaps the box's input/output shape per the schemas above.\n247\t\n248\t## Migration\n249\t\n250\tLegacy `data` boxes (the cosmetic-only kind) get rewritten by\n251\tthe loader. Two paths:\n252\t\n253\t- Boxes with a `ref` / `fn` (the call-equivalent shape they\n254\t  carry today) → rewrite `kind` to `call`. Behavior identical\n255\t  to current.\n256\t- Boxes without a `ref` / `fn` (rare — would be invalid today)\n257\t  → rewrite to `read` with no path; the validator then flags\n258\t  them so the user notices and fills in a path or literal.\n259\t\n260\tThe `data` kind is retired entirely. The schema rejects it\n261\tafter migration runs once.\n262\t\n263\t## Unwired-output discard rule\n264\t\n265\tThe general rule this issue makes use of, applicable to every\n266\tbox:\n267\t\n268\t> **If an output value is produced but no wire carries it\n269\t> downstream, the value is discarded.**\n270\t\n271\tA `write` box's done boolean is the most visible case — a user\n272\twho doesn't need a chain-after-write trigger leaves the output\n273\tunwired and the runtime drops the value. The rule already holds\n274\tinformally for every box; documenting it here (and in\n275\t`docs/001-architecture.md`) makes it explicit.\n276\t\n277\t## Suggested implementation sequence\n278\t\n279\t1. **Block on 317**: cross-language emit/write callbacks must be\n280\t   in place. Without them this issue degrades to plain-text IO.\n281\t2. **Schema** (`src/001-schema.lua`, `src/010-graph-loader.c`):\n282\t   accept `read` and `write`; retire `data`.\n283\t3. **Loader migration** (`src/003-loader.lua`): rewrite legacy\n284\t   `data` boxes per the migration section.\n285\t4. **Phase 2 executor** (`src/004-executor.lua`): handle `read`\n286\t   (literal or file) and `write` directly. Cross-language\n287\t   conversion uses the spec callbacks via the same path as\n288\t   call-box value transport.\n289\t5. **Phase 3 dispatch** (`src/012-dispatch.c`): same handling at\n290\t   the dispatch layer. `read`'s fan-out loops through downstream\n291\t   wires per spec; `write` looks up source-spec on its `value`\n292\t   input.\n293\t6. **Inspector** (`assets/js/004-inspector.js`): kind-specific\n294\t   layout per \"Inspector behavior\" above. The inline-value field\n295\t   for `read` is new; the port-hide-when-literal-value behavior\n296\t   is new and needs a small render-side hook in `draw_box`.\n297\t7. **Box rendering** (`assets/js/002-boxes.js`):\n298\t   - Add `read: '#4caf7d'` and `write: '#d4762a'` to `KIND_COLOR`.\n299\t   - Add `read`/`write` to the `KIND_HEADER` map from issue 236.\n300\t   - Honor `hide_port` flag (or equivalent) on the path input\n301\t     when the inline value is set on a `read` box.\n302\t8. **Documentation**: update `docs/001-architecture.md` with the\n303\t   new kinds, the unwired-output rule, and the language-aware\n304\t   IO behavior. Update the dispatch-layer info.md.\n305\t\n306\t## Open questions\n307\t\n308\t- **Output port labels** for `read` and `write`: `contents` for\n309\t  read, `done` for write — pick once, document, move on. Issue\n310\t  236 already established the per-kind output-label table; add\n311\t  these two rows.\n312\t- **Static path on `write`**: should `write` also accept an\n313\t  inline literal path on its `path` port (same way `read`\n314\t  does)? Probably yes — the use case \"save to a fixed location\n315\t  every time\" is common. Comes free if we apply the existing\n316\t  port-literal-value mechanism.\n317\t- **`read` with both literal and path set on disk** (a user who\n318\t  edits the JSON by hand and sets both): validator rejects, or\n319\t  literal-wins? Validator rejects — explicit error rather than\n320\t  hidden precedence.\n321\t- **Cross-language type fidelity** for the C spec: walking\n322\t  arbitrary C structs is rabbit-hole territory (issue 317\n323\t  tracks this). Until C's `native_to_json` handles structs,\n324\t  C-source `write` boxes are limited to scalar values. Same\n325\t  limitation issue 317 documents.\n326\t\n327\t## Relevant files\n328\t\n329\t- `src/001-schema.lua` — kind validation, new shapes\n330\t- `src/010-graph-loader.c` — C-side schema, migration\n331\t- `src/003-loader.lua` — legacy `data` rewrite\n332\t- `src/004-executor.lua` — phase 2 runtime handling\n333\t- `src/012-dispatch.c` — phase 3 dispatch primitives\n334\t- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — kind-specific inspector layout\n335\t- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — color, header, port-hide on literal\n336\t- `langs/{lua,c,bash}/spec.c` — `native_to_json` / `json_to_native`\n337\t  (issue 317 owns these)\n338\t- `docs/001-architecture.md` — kinds section, unwired-output rule\n339\t- `issues/317-spec-json-bridge-for-data-boxes.md` — hard dependency\n340\t- `issues/235-...completed/` — literal-replaces-port-name idea\n341\t  extended to \"literal hides port entirely\" here\n342\t- `issues/236-...completed/` — per-kind header/output-label map\n343\t- `issues/completed/216-read-file-box.md` — Lua-side read superseded\n344\t- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — phase 3 home for these\n345\t- `issues/completed/109-data-files-persistent-and-ephemeral.md` —\n346\t  `soramech-data` is a separate concern; not affected\n347\t\n348\t---\n349\t\n350\t## Historical proposals (superseded)\n351\t\n352\t### Revision 2 (single `data` kind, literal-or-file)\n353\t\n354\tProposed one unified source box: literal value typed in the\n355\tinspector OR file at `path`. Plus a separate `write` sink.\n356\tRejected because the source-and-sink-in-one-kind ambiguity\n357\tanalysis (above, in \"Why two kinds\") flagged real footguns —\n358\tthe `path`-input-without-`value` case silently reading from\n359\ta file the user meant to write to.\n360\t\n361\t### Revision 1 (`data` source + `file_write` sink)\n362\t\n363\tProposed a `data` kind (no inputs, just a `path` field; emits\n364\tfile bytes) and a separate write-sink. Renamed in revision 2\n365\tto `read` / `write` because verbs match what the boxes do\n366\tbetter than `data` does. Both revisions kept the same source\n367\t/ sink split.\n368\t\n369\tThe binary-data, atomic-write, JSON-parsing, and dispatch-layer\n370\thome questions all carry over unchanged through every\n371\trevision.\n372\t"
      }],
    "role":"user"
  }
}

Same for call boxes with no routing set\n     * (treated as plain). */\n    if (b->kind != BOX_CALL) return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n\n    switch (b->routing.kind) {\n        case ROUTING_PLAIN:\n            return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n\n        case ROUTING_COMPARATOR: {\n            double v = parse_double(out_bytes, out_size);\n            const char *branch =\n                (v < b->routing.comparand) ? \"lt\" :\n                (v > b->routing.comparand) ? \"gt\" : \"eq\";\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size, 0) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_ITERATOR: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1) {\n                /* No counter slot or zero outputs — fall back to plain. */\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            /* The counter is both the branch selector AND the order\n             * tag for the consumer slot (issue 304 cell-tagged\n             * ordering).       "content":"     * output — shares the box's language. Data boxes and\n     * file_write boxes don't constrain (they emit/consume raw\n     * bytes that any spec interprets uniformly).\n     *\n     * Computed in graph_load (not graph_attach_runtime) because\n     * it's purely topology-derived and doesn't need the slot\n     * store or registry. The dispatch action picks\n     * `spec->invoke_native` when this flag is set, falling back to\n     * `invoke_json` or `invoke`. Our current specs all leave\n     * invoke_native NULL so the fallback runs and behaviour is\n     * unchanged — but the infrastructure is in place. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n        b->input_edge_native  = NULL;\n        b->output_edge_native = NULL;\n        b->use_native_invoke  = 0;\n        if (b->kind != BOX_CALL || !b->lang) continue;\n\n        /* Allocate per-port input bits and per-connection output\n         * bits. malloc rather than calloc — we fill every entry\n         * explicitly below. */\n        if (b->n_inputs > 0) {\n            b->input_edge_native = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->input_edge_native) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return NULL; }\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_inputs; j++) b->input_edge_native[j] = 0;\n        }\n        if (b->n_connections > 0) {\n            b->output_edge_native = malloc((size_t)b->n_connections * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->output_edge_native) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return NULL; }\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) b->output_edge_native[j] = 0;\n        }\n\n        /* Outgoing edges: for each connection, the consumer's lang\n         * is native iff it's also a call box in this box's\n         * language. Data / file_write consumers are not native\n         * (they don't carry a language). */\n        int all_outs_native = 1;\n        for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) {\n            int dst = b->connections[j].to_box_idx;\n            if (dst < 0) { all_outs_native = 0; continue; }\n            const box_t *c = &g->boxes[dst];\n            int native = (c->kind == BOX_CALL && c->lang\n                          && strcmp(c->lang, b->lang) == 0);\n            b->output_edge_native[j] = native;\n            if (!native) all_outs_native = 0;\n        }\n\n        /* Incoming edges: for each input port, scan every producer\n         * in the graph; the port is native iff at least one\n         * producer feeds it AND every feeding producer shares this\n         * box's language. (A mixed-language fan-in downgrades the\n         * port to JSON for the whole port — the slot can carry only\n         * one format, and JSON is the common denominator.) */\n        int all_ins_native = 1;\n        for (int port = 0; port < b->n_inputs; port++) {\n            int any_producer = 0;\n            int all_native   = 1;\n            for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes; p++) {\n                const box_t *prod = &g->boxes[p];\n                for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                    if (prod->connections[k].to_box_idx != i)        continue;\n                    if (prod->connections[k].to_input_idx != port)   continue;\n                    any_producer = 1;\n                    int native = (prod->kind == BOX_CALL && prod->lang\n                                  && strcmp(prod->lang, b->lang) == 0);\n                    if (!native) all_native = 0;\n                }\n            }\n            b->input_edge_native[port] = (any_producer && all_native) ? 1 : 0;\n            if (!b->input_edge_native[port]) all_ins_native = 0;\n        }\n\n        /* Retain the per-box bit for dispatch sites that haven't\n         * been migrated to per-edge consultation yet. Only true\n         * when EVERY edge in both directions is native. */\n        b->use_native_invoke = (all_ins_native && all_outs_native) ? 1 : 0;\n    }\n    return g;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ graph_destroy() */\nvoid graph_destroy(graph_t *g)\n{\n    if (!g) return;\n    if (g->boxes) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n            free(g->boxes[i].inputs);\n            free(g->boxes[i].connections);\n            free(g->boxes[i].input_slot_ids);\n            free(g->boxes[i].input_slot_modes);\n            free(g->boxes[i].input_edge_native);\n            free(g->boxes[i].output_edge_native);\n            free((double *)g->boxes[i].routing.weights);\n        }\n        free(g->boxes);\n    }\n    free(g->languages);    /* element strings live in the arena */\n    free(g->map_dir);\n    json_arena_destroy(g->arena);",

    "originalFile":"/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n * to drive a run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n * whether to abort or surface the error.\n *\n * What's implemented now: phases 1 (directory walk), 2 (JSON\n * parse), and the first part of 3 (per-box schema validation —\n * kind valid, id unique, kind-specific required fields present,\n * routing schema validated).\n *\n * What's deferred to follow-ons within 305:\n *  - Phase 4: topology validation. Connections currently store\n *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n *\n * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,         /* runs a function via a language spec        */\n    BOX_DATA,         /* file source — dispatch reads `path` at run */\n    BOX_FILE_WRITE,   /* file sink  — dispatch writes inputs at run */\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* Weighted routing: arena-owned double array of n_outputs\n     * entries. Normalised at runtime. NULL for other kinds. */\n    const double  *weights;\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics; resolved integer\n * indices are filled in by the topology pass and let the dispatch\n * layer (issue 304) avoid string lookups at runtime. */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input;     /* destination port name                   */\n    const char *from_branch;  /* NULL for plain output; else branch name */\n    int         to_box_idx;   /* resolved index into graph->boxes        */\n    int         to_input_idx; /* resolved index into target's inputs[]   */\n} connection_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Box */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char    *id;\n    box_kind_t     kind;\n\n    /* Call boxes */\n    const char    *lang;          /* \"lua\" / \"c\" / \"bash\" / NULL    */\n    const char    *ref;           /* source file (call only)        */\n    const char    *fn;            /* function name (call only)      */\n    routing_t      routing;       /* call only                      */\n    int            output_capacity; /* 0 means variable-size        */\n\n    /* Data boxes */\n    const char    *path;          /* file path (data only)          */\n\n    /* Common */\n    int            n_inputs;\n    input_decl_t  *inputs;\n    int            n_connections;\n    connection_t  *connections;\n\n    /* Runtime state — populated by graph_attach_runtime, left at\n     * defaults (-1 / NULL / 0) by graph_load alone. */\n    int            spec_idx;       /* index into the spec registry; -1 if no spec  */\n    int           *input_slot_ids; /* n_inputs entries; -1 if not allocated yet    */\n    int           *input_slot_modes;/* 0 = PEEK (1-cell), 1 = POP (N-cell)         */\n    int            counter_slot_id;/* atomic-counter slot for iterator routing; -1 */\n    int            multi_spawn;    /* 1 if the box may fire many times in one run  */\n\n    /* 312 per-edge fast-path classification.\n     *\n     * One bit per input port: true iff the producer feeding that\n     * port shares this box's language. When set, the dispatch\n     * passes the slot's bytes to invoke_native as-is; when cleared\n     * the dispatch calls json_to_native first.\n     *\n     * One bit per outgoing connection (not per output port — a\n     * single output may fan to consumers of different languages):\n     * true iff the consumer on the other end of that connection\n     * shares this box's language. When set, push native bytes\n     * directly; when cleared, call native_to_json first and push\n     * JSON. */\n    int           *input_edge_native;   /* n_inputs entries, or NULL              */\n    int           *output_edge_native;  /* n_connections entries, or NULL         */\n\n    /* The earlier per-box approximation, retained until the\n     * dispatch fully switches to per-edge consultation. Computed as\n     * (all input_edge_native bits set) && (all output_edge_native\n     * bits set) — i.e. true only for boxes inside a same-language\n     * island with no cross-language neighbours. */\n    int            use_native_invoke;\n} box_t;\n\n/* Slot mode constants used by box_t.input_slot_modes[]. */\n#define SLOT_MODE_PEEK 0\n#define SLOT_MODE_POP  1\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Graph */\ntypedef struct graph graph_t;\n\n/* Read a map directory and build the graph. Returns NULL on any\n * failure and sets *err to a malloc'd \"<file>:<line>: <message>\"\n * diagnostic. The caller frees *err. */\ngraph_t *graph_load(const char *map_dir, char **err);\n\n/* Free the graph and every byte it owns. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid     graph_destroy(graph_t *g);\n\n/* Accessors. */\nconst char  *graph_name        (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_description (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_entry_box_id(const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_map_dir     (const graph_t *g);\nint          graph_n_boxes     (const graph_t *g);\nconst box_t *graph_box         (const graph_t *g, int i);\nconst box_t *graph_box_by_id   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n\n/* Find a box's index by id; -1 if missing. */\nint          graph_box_index   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n\n/* Distinct language names used by call boxes in the map (filled\n * in by graph_attach_runtime). The pool's spec init can use this\n * to skip workers for specs the map doesn't actually use. */\nint          graph_n_languages (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_language    (const graph_t *g, int i);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Runtime attach (phase 5 + 7)\n *\n * Allocates one slot per input port for every box and resolves each\n * call box's language spec from the registry. After this call, the\n * dispatch layer can read inputs via `box->input_slot_ids[i]` and\n * invoke the spec via `spec_registry_at(r, box->spec_idx)`.\n *\n * Slot defaults for this iteration:\n *   - cell_capacity = `default_cell_bytes` (or 4096 if 0)\n *   - n_cells = 1 (peek mode)\n *   - flags = 0\n *\n * Iterator-fed wires and the multi-cell pop mode land in a follow-on\n * — they need compile-time wire classification (issue 305 phase 5\n * proper) that this iteration ducks. Returns 0 on success, -1 with\n * *err set on the first resolution or allocation failure. */\nstruct slot_store;        /* opaque forward decl */\nstruct spec_registry;     /* opaque forward decl */\nint graph_attach_runtime(graph_t *g,\n                         struct slot_store    *slots,\n                         struct spec_registry *specs,\n                         int                   default_cell_bytes,\n                         char                **err);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H */\n",

The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n * whether to abort or surface the error.\n *\n * What's implemented now: phases 1 (directory walk), 2 (JSON\n * parse), and the first part of 3 (per-box schema validation —\n * kind valid, id unique, kind-specific required fields present,\n * routing schema validated).\n *\n * What's deferred to follow-ons within 305:\n *  - Phase 4: topology validation. Connections currently store\n *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n *\n * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,    /* runs a function via a language spec                */\n    BOX_READ,    /* value source — inline literal or file at `path`    */\n    BOX_WRITE,   /* file sink — writes one input, emits \"true\" downstream */\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* Weighted routing: arena-owned double array of n_outputs\n     * entries. Normalised at runtime. NULL for other kinds. */\n    const double  *weights;\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics; resolved integer\n * indices are filled in by the topology pass and let the dispatch\n * layer (issue 304) avoid string lookups at runtime. */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input;     /* destination port name                   */\n    const char *from_branch;  /* NULL for plain output; else branch name */\n    int         to_box_idx;   /* resolved index into graph->boxes        */\n    int         to_input_idx; /* resolved index into target's inputs[]   */\n} connection_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Box */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char    *id;\n    box_kind_t     kind;\n\n    /* Call boxes */\n    const char    *lang;          /* \"lua\" / \"c\" / \"bash\" / NULL    */\n    const char    *ref;           /* source file (call only)        */\n    const char    *fn;            /* function name (call only)      */\n    routing_t      routing;       /* call only                      */\n    int            output_capacity; /* 0 means variable-size        */\n\n    /* Data boxes */\n    const char    *path;          /* file path (data only)          */\n\n    /* Common */\n    int            n_inputs;\n    input_decl_t  *inputs;\n    int            n_connections;\n    connection_t  *connections;\n\n    /* Runtime state — populated by graph_attach_runtime, left at\n     * defaults (-1 / NULL / 0) by graph_load alone. */\n    int            spec_idx;       /* index into the spec registry; -1 if no spec  */\n    int           *input_slot_ids; /* n_inputs entries; -1 if not allocated yet    */\n    int           *input_slot_modes;/* 0 = PEEK (1-cell), 1 = POP (N-cell)         */\n    int            counter_slot_id;/* atomic-counter slot for iterator routing; -1 */\n    int            multi_spawn;    /* 1 if the box may fire many times in one run  */\n\n    /* 312 per-edge fast-path classification.\n     *\n     * One bit per input port: true iff the producer feeding that\n     * port shares this box's language. When set, the dispatch\n     * passes the slot's bytes to invoke_native as-is; when cleared\n     * the dispatch calls json_to_native first.\n     *\n     * One bit per outgoing connection (not per output port — a\n     * single output may fan to consumers of different languages):\n     * true iff the consumer on the other end of that connection\n     * shares this box's language. When set, push native bytes\n     * directly; when cleared, call native_to_json first and push\n     * JSON. */\n    int           *input_edge_native;   /* n_inputs entries, or NULL              */\n    int           *output_edge_native;  /* n_connections entries, or NULL         */\n\n    /* The earlier per-box approximation, retained until the\n     * dispatch fully switches to per-edge consultation. Computed as\n     * (all input_edge_native bits set) && (all output_edge_native\n     * bits set) — i.e. true only for boxes inside a same-language\n     * island with no cross-language neighbours. */\n    int            use_native_invoke;\n} box_t;\n\n/* Slot mode constants used by box_t.input_slot_modes[]. */\n#define SLOT_MODE_PEEK 0\n#define SLOT_MODE_POP  1\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Graph */\ntypedef struct graph graph_t;\n\n/* Read a map directory and build the graph. Returns NULL on any\n * failure and sets *err to a malloc'd \"<file>:<line>: <message>\"\n * diagnostic. The caller frees *err. */\ngraph_t *graph_load(const char *map_dir, char **err);\n\n/* Free the graph and every byte it owns. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid     graph_destroy(graph_t *g);\n\n/* Accessors. */\nconst char  *graph_name        (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_description (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_entry_box_id(const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_map_dir     (const graph_t *g);\nint          graph_n_boxes     (const graph_t *g);\nconst box_t *graph_box         (const graph_t *g, int i);\nconst box_t *graph_box_by_id   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n\n/* Find a box's index by id; -1 if missing. */\nint          graph_box_index   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n\n/* Distinct language names used by call boxes in the map (filled\n * in by graph_attach_runtime). The pool's spec init can use this\n * to skip workers for specs the map doesn't actually use. */\nint          graph_n_languages (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_language    (const graph_t *g, int i);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Runtime attach (phase 5 + 7)\n *\n * Allocates one slot per input port for every box and resolves each\n * call box's language spec from the registry. After this call, the\n * dispatch layer can read inputs via `box->input_slot_ids[i]` and\n * invoke the spec via `spec_registry_at(r, box->spec_idx)`.\n *\n * Slot defaults for this iteration:\n *   - cell_capacity = `default_cell_bytes` (or 4096 if 0)\n *   - n_cells = 1 (peek mode)\n *   - flags = 0\n *\n * Iterator-fed wires and the multi-cell pop mode land in a follow-on\n * — they need compile-time wire classification (issue 305 phase 5\n * proper) that this iteration ducks. Returns 0 on success, -1 with\n * *err set on the first resolution or allocation failure. */\nstruct slot_store;        /* opaque forward decl */\nstruct spec_registry;     /* opaque forward decl */\nint graph_attach_runtime(graph_t *g,\n                         struct slot_store    *slots,\n                         struct spec_registry *specs,\n                         int                   default_cell_bytes,\n                         char                **err);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H */\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.h"
  },
