          "new_string":"/* {{{ do_read_box() — emit the box's value */\n/* Precedence (issue 229):\n *   1. Inline `value` literal — copied verbatim, no file IO.\n *   2. Static `path` field — read that file from disk.\n *   3. `path` input wire — would arrive in the box's input slot;\n *      not exercised by current fixtures but supported by reading\n *      slot[port=\"path\"] when no static path is set.\n *   4. Otherwise, error — the box has nothing to emit. */\nstatic int do_read_box(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                       char *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size)\n{\n    /* (1) inline literal */\n    if (b->value) {\n        int n = (int)strlen(b->value);\n        if (n > out_capacity) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: read box '%s' literal (%d bytes) \"\n                            \"exceeds output capacity %d\\n\",\n                    b->id, n, out_capacity);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        memcpy(out_buf, b->value, (size_t)n);\n        *out_size = n;\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    /* (2) static path. The (3) \"path-from-input\" form is left as a\n     * future slice — the inputs[] slot needs to be peeked first.\n     * Today's fixtures all use the static path. */\n    const char *path_str = b->path;\n    if (!path_str) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: read box '%s' has neither value \"\n                        \"nor path\\n\", b->id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    char *full = resolve_path(ctx, path_str);\n    if (!full) return -1;\n    FILE *fp = fopen(full, \"rb\");\n    if (!fp) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: read box '%s': cannot open '%s'\\n\",\n                b->id, full);\n        free(full);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    int total = 0;\n    while (total < out_capacity) {\n        size_t r = fread(out_buf + total, 1,\n                         (size_t)(out_capacity - total), fp);\n        if (r == 0) break;\n        total += (int)r;\n    }\n    fclose(fp);\n    free(full);\n    *out_size = total;\n    return 0;\n}",
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"/* {{{ do_data_box() — read file from box->path */\nstatic int do_data_box(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                       char *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size)\n{\n    if (!b->path) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: data box '%s' missing path\\n\", b->id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    char *full = resolve_path(ctx, b->path);\n    if (!full) return -1;\n    FILE *fp = fopen(full, \"rb\");\n    if (!fp) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: data box '%s': cannot open '%s'\\n\",\n                b->id, full);\n        free(full);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    int total = 0;\n    while (total < out_capacity) {\n        size_t r = fread(out_buf + total, 1,\n                         (size_t)(out_capacity - total), fp);\n        if (r == 0) break;\n        total += (int)r;\n    }\n    fclose(fp);\n    free(full);\n    *out_size = total;\n    return 0;\n}",

A `write` box with no downstream wire\n * still produces the boolean; the dispatch fans to zero consumers\n * and the value is discarded (unwired-output rule). */\nstatic int do_write_box(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b, int task_id,\n                        char *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size)\n{\n    char       *bufs[16]  = {0};\n    const void *datas[16] = {0};\n    int         sizes[16] = {0};\n    int failed = 0;\n    int n_present = read_inputs(ctx, b, bufs, datas, sizes,\n                                ctx->default_out_capacity, &failed);\n    emit_input_events(ctx, task_id, bufs, sizes, n_present);\n    int path_idx = -1, value_idx = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(b->inputs[i].name, \"path\")  == 0) path_idx  = i;\n        if (strcmp(b->inputs[i].name, \"value\") == 0) value_idx = i;\n    }\n    if (failed || path_idx < 0 || value_idx < 0\n            || path_idx >= n_present || value_idx >= n_present) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) free(bufs[i]);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    /* Make NUL-terminated copy of the path. */\n    char *path = malloc((size_t)sizes[path_idx] + 1);\n    if (!path) { for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) free(bufs[i]); return -1; }\n    memcpy(path, datas[path_idx], (size_t)sizes[path_idx]);\n    path[sizes[path_idx]] = '\\0';\n\n    char *full = resolve_path(ctx, path);\n    free(path);\n    if (!full) { for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) free(bufs[i]); return -1; }\n\n    FILE *fp = fopen(full, \"wb\");\n    free(full);\n    int rc = 0;\n    if (!fp) rc = -1;\n    else {\n        size_t want = (size_t)sizes[value_idx];\n        if (fwrite(datas[value_idx], 1, want, fp) != want) rc = -1;\n        fclose(fp);\n    }\n    for (int i = 0;     "originalFile":"# 010-graph-loader.c — public surface\n\nC graph loader (phase 3). Replaces `src/003-loader.lua`.\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- `graph_t *graph_load(const char *map_dir, char **err)` — read +\n  parse + validate. Returns NULL on any failure and sets `*err` to\n  a malloc'd `\"<file>:<line>: <message>\"` diagnostic. The caller\n  frees `*err`.\n- `void graph_destroy(graph_t *g)` — frees every byte the graph\n  owns (the box and connection arrays, the input declarations, the\n  underlying JSON arena holding every string).\n\n## Accessors\n\n- `const char *graph_name(g)`\n- `const char *graph_description(g)`\n- `const char *graph_entry_box_id(g)`\n- `int          graph_n_boxes(g)`\n- `const box_t *graph_box(g, i)`\n- `const box_t *graph_box_by_id(g, id)`\n\n## Public types\n\n- `box_kind_t` — `BOX_CALL` / `BOX_DATA` / `BOX_FILE_WRITE`.\n- `routing_kind_t` — `ROUTING_PLAIN` / `ROUTING_COMPARATOR` /\n  `ROUTING_ITERATOR`; randomizer / weighted / distributor enum\n  values exist but the parser doesn't accept them yet.\n- `routing_t` — `kind` plus per-kind params (`n_outputs`,\n  `comparand`).\n- `input_decl_t` — `name`, `type`, `literal`, `optional`.\n- `connection_t` — outgoing connection. Stores string refs\n  (`to_box`, `to_input`); resolved-to-integer-index forms come in\n  the topology iteration.\n- `box_t` — all of the above per box.\n\n## Schema currently enforced\n\n- `meta.json` must be a JSON object containing at least `name`.\n- Every file under `boxes/` ending in `.json` is a box file with a\n  top-level object, `id` (string), `kind` ∈ `{call, data, file_write}`.\n- `call` boxes: require `ref` and `routing`. `fn` is optional (a\n  language without function-name dispatch is fine). `lang` is\n  optional too — falls back to inference from `ref` extension once\n  the spec registry lands.\n- `data` boxes: require `path`; no `ref` / `fn` / `routing`.\n- `file_write` boxes: no kind-specific required fields beyond\n  inputs.\n- `routing.kind` ∈ `{plain, comparator, iterator}` (issue 233's\n  shipped surface). `comparator` requires `comparand` (number or\n  string-form number per the issue's example shape).\n  `iterator` requires `n_outputs` (>= 1).\n- Box ids must be unique across the map. O(n²) scan; n is small.\n\n## What's NOT here (deferred to follow-on iterations within 305)\n\n- **Phase 4 — topology validation.** Connection endpoints aren't\n  resolved to integer indices yet; we don't verify that every\n  `to_box` refers to a real box, nor that the `to_input` matches a\n  declared port. Cycle detection (excluding iterator-rooted\n  cycles) lands here too.\n- **Phase 5 — slot size class enumeration.** The slot store's\n  `slot_alloc` consumes a `cell_capacity`; the loader's job is to\n  scan box outputs and enumerate the distinct sizes the graph\n  needs.\n- **Phase 6 — entry-box detection.** Boxes with no inputs (or\n  inputs fed only by `data` boxes) get auto-detected as entry\n  points.\n- **Phase 7 — language enumeration.** Walk every call box,\n  collect distinct `lang` values, hand the set to the spec\n  registry.\n- The remaining routing kinds (`randomizer`, `weighted`,\n  `distributor`) — issue 233 deferred them to their own\n  follow-ons; the parser rejects them with a precise message.\n\nNone of these block issues 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n\n## Related\n\n- Issue 305 — design.\n- Issue 233 — unified routing schema this loader implements.\n- Issue 229 — data / file_write box kinds.\n- Issue 314 — the JSON parser this depends on.\n- Issue 302 — slot store; the loader will eventually hand size\n  class enumeration to it.\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.info.md"
  },

    "replaceAll":false,
    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline file_write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"who → World\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n    \"input → 5\" \\\n    \"double → 10\" \\\n    \"addone → 11\" \\\n    \"shout → 11!\"\n\npipeline_output_check\ncompile_pipeline_check\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ parser_tests() — issue 232: unit tests for langs/<lang>/parser.js\n# Run Node's built-in test runner over each per-language parser test\n# file and fold the result into the surrounding pass/fail counters.\n# Each .mjs file is one logical \"test\" from this script's perspective;\n# Node prints its own subtest breakdown on failure for the diagnostic.\nparser_tests() {\n    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"  %-44s SKIP — node not installed\\n\" \"parser tests (lua, bash)\"\n        return\n    fi\n    for tf in \"$DIR/tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/234-language-spec-js-test.mjs\"; do\n        local label\n        label=$(basename \"$tf\")\n        printf \"  %-44s \" \"$label\"\n        local out\n        out=$(SORAMECH_DIR=\"$DIR\" node --test \"$tf\" 2>&1)\n        local rc=$?\n        if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL\\n\"\n            echo \"$out\" | sed 's/^/      /'\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"$label: node --test exit=$rc\")\n        fi\n    done\n}\nparser_tests\n# }}}\n\necho\necho \"  $pass passed, $fail failed\"\n\nif [[ $fail -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo\n    echo \"  failures:\"\n    for f in \"${failures[@]}\"; do\n        echo \"    - $f\"\n    done\nfi\n\nexit $fail\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/scripts/run-tests.sh"
  },

      "content":"-- Schema definitions and validators for SoraMech map files.\n-- Validates box files, meta.json, and drivers.json against the spec\n-- in docs/001-architecture.md. Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, data = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_branches\n-- null/nil means no comparator (single wire); the three strings are comparator outputs.\nlocal valid_branches = { lt = true, eq = true, gt = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- from_branch is nil (no comparator) or one of \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"\n    if c.from_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.from_branch ~= nil and not valid_branches[c.from_branch] then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] 'from_branch' must be nil, 'lt', 'eq', or 'gt'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be 'call' or 'data')\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" or box.kind == \"data\" then\n        -- iterator boxes (issue 221) are a pure routing primitive: input\n        -- copies straight to a chosen output, no language function is\n        -- invoked. Such a box has no ref/fn — only `iterator_outputs`,\n        -- an ordered list of output slot names. Otherwise ref is required.\n        local is_iterator = box.iterator_outputs ~= nil\n        if not is_iterator then\n            if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n                err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n            end\n        end\n        if box.iterator_outputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.iterator_outputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.iterator_outputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- variadic_inputs: optional list of base names; each name must\n        -- correspond to a series of inputs named \"<base>_<index>\" in\n        -- box.inputs (the editor maintains this; we only check the\n        -- shape here). See issue 217 part B.\n        if box.variadic_inputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.variadic_inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.variadic_inputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        -- has_output: optional; absence means \"true\" (default behavior).\n        -- false marks a sink box whose function has no return values\n        -- (issue 226); the runtime treats such boxes as terminal and the\n        -- editor hides the output port and inspector output section.\n        if box.has_output ~= nil and type(box.has_output) ~= \"boolean\" then\n            err(errors, \"'has_output' must be a boolean\")\n        end\n        -- Per-port `optional` flag (issue 230). Absent means false: the\n        -- port is required and must be either wired or carry a literal\n        -- value. The wire/literal/optional triple-check happens at the\n        -- graph level (validate-map.lua and the editor's compile path),\n        -- not here — this only validates per-port shape.\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) == \"table\" then\n            for i, p in ipairs(box.inputs) do\n                if type(p) == \"table\" and p.optional ~= nil and type(p.optional) ~= \"boolean\" then\n                    err(errors, \"'inputs[\" .. i .. \"].optional' must be a boolean\")\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ check_input_bindings\n-- Graph-level check from issue 230: every input port on every box\n-- must be in one of three states by compile time —\n--   1. a wire is connected to it\n--   2. a literal `value` is set on it\n--   3. it carries `optional: true`\n-- Otherwise the box would silently receive a missing arg at runtime\n-- and the bug would only surface where the function happens to\n-- reference it. do\n        local box = boxes[id]\n        for _, p in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n            local has_wire    = wired[id .. \"\\0\" .. p.name] == true\n            local has_literal = p.value ~= nil and p.value ~= \"\"\n            local is_optional = p.optional == true\n            if not (has_wire or has_literal or is_optional) then\n                err(errors, \"box '\" .. id .. \"': input     "originalFile":"-- Schema definitions and validators for SoraMech map files.\n-- Validates box files, meta.json, and drivers.json against the spec\n-- in docs/001-architecture.md. Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, data = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_branches\n-- null/nil means no comparator (single wire); the three strings are comparator outputs.\nlocal valid_branches = { lt = true, eq = true, gt = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- from_branch is nil (no comparator) or one of \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"\n    if c.from_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.from_branch ~= nil and not valid_branches[c.from_branch] then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] 'from_branch' must be nil, 'lt', 'eq', or 'gt'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be 'call' or 'data')\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" or box.kind == \"data\" then\n        -- iterator boxes (issue 221) are a pure routing primitive: input\n        -- copies straight to a chosen output, no language function is\n        -- invoked. Such a box has no ref/fn — only `iterator_outputs`,\n        -- an ordered list of output slot names. Otherwise ref is required.\n        local is_iterator = box.iterator_outputs ~= nil\n        if not is_iterator then\n            if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n                err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n            end\n        end\n        if box.iterator_outputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.iterator_outputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.iterator_outputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- variadic_inputs: optional list of base names; each name must\n        -- correspond to a series of inputs named \"<base>_<index>\" in\n        -- box.inputs (the editor maintains this; we only check the\n        -- shape here). See issue 217 part B.\n        if box.variadic_inputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.variadic_inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.variadic_inputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        -- has_output: optional; absence means \"true\" (default behavior).\n        -- false marks a sink box whose function has no return values\n        -- (issue 226); the runtime treats such boxes as terminal and the\n        -- editor hides the output port and inspector output section.\n        if box.has_output ~= nil and type(box.has_output) ~= \"boolean\" then\n            err(errors, \"'has_output' must be a boolean\")\n        end\n        -- Per-port `optional` flag (issue 230). Absent means false: the\n        -- port is required and must be either wired or carry a literal\n        -- value. The wire/literal/optional triple-check happens at the\n        -- graph level (validate-map.lua and the editor's compile path),\n        -- not here — this only validates per-port shape.\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) == \"table\" then\n            for i, p in ipairs(box.inputs) do\n                if type(p) == \"table\" and p.optional ~= nil and type(p.optional) ~= \"boolean\" then\n                    err(errors, \"'inputs[\" .. i .. \"].optional' must be a boolean\")\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ check_input_bindings\n-- Graph-level check from issue 230: every input port on every box\n-- must be in one of three states by compile time —\n--   1. a wire is connected to it\n--   2. a literal `value` is set on it\n--   3. it carries `optional: true`\n-- Otherwise the box would silently receive a missing arg at runtime\n-- and the bug would only surface where the function happens to\n-- reference it. The check fails loud and points at the exact box +\n-- port instead.\n--\n-- `boxes` is a table mapping box-id → box record (the shape the\n-- editor cache and the phase 2 loader's graph use). Returns an\n-- array of error strings; empty array means OK.\nfunction M.check_input_bindings(boxes)\n    local errors = {}\n\n    -- precompute: for each (to_box, to_input) → true if a wire targets it.\n    -- Connections live on both endpoints (issue 228), so scanning every\n    -- box's connection list overcounts but doesn't miss anything.\n    local wired = {}\n    for _, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.to_box and c.to_input then\n                wired[c.to_box .. \"\\0\" .. c.to_input] = true\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- stable per-box iteration for predictable error ordering\n    local ids = {}\n    for id, _ in pairs(boxes) do ids[#ids + 1] = id end\n    table.sort(ids)\n\n    for _, id in ipairs(ids) do\n        local box = boxes[id]\n        for _, p in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n            local has_wire    = wired[id .. \"\\0\" .. p.name] == true\n            local has_literal = p.value ~= nil and p.value ~= \"\"\n            local is_optional = p.optional == true\n            if not (has_wire or has_literal or is_optional) then\n                err(errors, \"box '\" .. id .. \"': input '\" .. tostring(p.name) ..\n                    \"' has no wire, no literal, and is not optional\")\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

Otherwise ref is required.\n        local is_iterator = box.iterator_outputs ~= nil\n        if not is_iterator then\n            if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n                err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n            end\n        end\n        if box.iterator_outputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.iterator_outputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.iterator_outputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- variadic_inputs: optional list of base names; each name must\n        -- correspond to a series of inputs named \"<base>_<index>\" in\n        -- box.inputs (the editor maintains this; we only check the\n        -- shape here). See issue 217 part B.\n        if box.variadic_inputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.variadic_inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.variadic_inputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        -- has_output: optional; absence means \"true\" (default behavior).\n        -- false marks a sink box whose function has no return values\n        -- (issue 226); the runtime treats such boxes as terminal and the\n        -- editor hides the output port and inspector output section.\n        if box.has_output ~= nil and type(box.has_output) ~= \"boolean\" then\n            err(errors, \"'has_output' must be a boolean\")\n        end\n        -- Per-port `optional` flag (issue 230). Absent means false: the\n        -- port is required and must be either wired or carry a literal\n        -- value. Returns an\n-- array of error strings; empty array means OK.\nfunction M.check_input_bindings(boxes)\n    local errors = {}\n\n    -- precompute: for each (to_box, to_input) → true if a wire targets it.\n    -- Connections live on both endpoints (issue 228), so scanning every\n    -- box's connection list overcounts but doesn't miss anything.\n    local wired = {}\n    for _, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.to_box and c.to_input then\n                wired[c.to_box .. \"\\0\" .. c.to_input] = true\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- stable per-box iteration for predictable error ordering\n    local ids = {}\n    for id, _ in pairs(boxes) do ids[#ids + 1] = id end\n    table.sort(ids)\n\n    for _, id in ipairs(ids) nil and p.value ~= \"\"\n            local is_optional = p.optional == true\n            if not (has_wire or has_literal or is_optional) then\n                err(errors, \"box '\" .. id .. \"': input '\" .. tostring(p.name) ..\n                    \"' has no wire, no literal, and is not optional\")\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

Add a row when a new kind ships.\n  const KIND_HEADER = {\n    branch:     'branch',\n    data:       'data',\n    comparator: 'comparator',\n    iterator:   'iterator',\n  };\n\n  // Comparator branch colors: lt=orange, eq=blue, gt=green\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // boxes: { [id]: box_data }\n  let boxes = {};\n\n  // {{{ default_header\n  // The box header text used when `box.label` is unset (issue 236).\n  // Three cases:\n  //   call    — basename of `ref`, the source file the box calls\n  //   other   — the kind name, plain\n  //   unknown — fall back to the box id so nothing renders blank\n  // Exported so the inspector can show it as the label-field\n  // placeholder, keeping the inspector and canvas in sync about\n  // \"what would render if I left this empty\".\n  function default_header(box) {\n    if (box.kind === 'call' && box.ref) {\n      const parts = String(box.ref).split('/');\n      return parts[parts.length - 1] || box.ref;\n    }\n    return KIND_HEADER[box.kind] || box.kind || box.id;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ output_label_text\n  // Picks the string drawn to the LEFT of an output port dot\n  // (issue 236). ## [779]

```json
{
  "userType":"external",
  "parentUuid":"9ab59a13-c454-4c45-b599-870fbaead1f2",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-20T04:24:06.665Z",
  "isSidechain":false,
  "cwd":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "type":"text",
    "file":{
      "content":"  //   - value set, no wire         → the value (what the box does)\n  //   - value too long / multiline → first line, truncated with …\n  // The two-branch decision is the visible heart of issue 235: a\n  // reader scanning the map should see the data the box operates on,\n  // not the parameter slot it sits in.\n  function port_label_text(box, i) {\n    const p = box.inputs[i];\n    const has_value = p.value !== undefined && p.value !== null && p.value !== '';\n    if (!has_value)                              return p.name;\n    if (port_has_incoming_wire(box, p.name))     return p.name;\n    const raw        = String(p.value);\n    const first_line = raw.split('\\n')[0];\n    const multiline  = first_line.length < raw.length;\n    if (first_line.length > MAX_LABEL_CHARS) {\n      return first_line.slice(0, MAX_LABEL_CHARS - 1) + '…';\n    }\n    if (multiline) return first_line + '…';\n    return first_line;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ box_height\n  function box_height(box) {\n    const n_in  = (box.inputs || []).length;\n    // Output rows: iterator boxes have N named slots (issue 221);\n    // comparator active: 3 dots (lt/eq/gt); sink: 0; otherwise 1.\n    let n_out;\n    if (box.iterator_outputs) {\n      n_out = box.iterator_outputs.length;\n    } else if (box.has_output === false) {\n      n_out = 0;\n    } else if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      n_out = 3;\n    } else {\n      n_out = 1;\n    }\n    return Math.max(MIN_BOX_H, BOX_HEADER + Math.max(n_in, n_out) * PORT_ROW_H + 8);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ port_positions\n  // Returns world-space {x,y} for each port dot on a box.\n  // Output side: null-named single dot when no comparand; 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' dots when comparand set.\n  function port_positions(box) {\n    const bx = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const by = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const h  = box_height(box);\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n\n    const in_pts = inputs.map((p, i) => ({\n      name: p.name, side: 'input',\n      x: bx,\n      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n    }));\n\n    let out_pts;\n    if (box.has_output === false) {\n      // sink box — function has no return values (issue 226). No output\n      // port, no wire-grab target, nothing for the inspector to render.\n      out_pts = [];\n    } else if (box.iterator_outputs) {\n      // iterator box (issue 221) — N named output dots stacked down\n      // the right edge, one per declared slot. Slot names land in the\n      // `name` field, so the wire's `from_branch` will pick them up\n      // exactly like a comparator branch name.\n      out_pts = box.iterator_outputs.map((slot, i) => ({\n        name: slot, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      // three comparator dots\n      out_pts = ['lt', 'eq', 'gt'].map((branch, i) => ({\n        name: branch, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else {\n      // single output dot, vertically centered in the box\n      out_pts = [{\n        name: null, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + h / 2,\n      }];\n    }\n\n    return { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_box\n  function draw_box(ctx, box, selected) {\n    const x = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const y = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const w = BOX_W;\n    const h = box_height(box);\n    const kind  = box.kind || 'call';\n    const color = KIND_COLOR[kind] || '#888';\n\n    // shadow when selected\n    if (selected) {\n      ctx.shadowColor = color;\n      ctx.shadowBlur  = 12;\n    }\n\n    // body\n    ctx.fillStyle   = '#1e2130';\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? color : '#3a3f55';\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2 : 1;\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 6);\n    ctx.fill();\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    ctx.shadowBlur = 0;\n\n    // header bar\n    ctx.fillStyle = color + '33';\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, BOX_HEADER, [6, 6, 0, 0]);\n    ctx.fill();\n\n    // label — user override wins; otherwise the kind-driven default\n    // (issue 236): basename of ref for call boxes, plain kind name\n    // for everything else.\n    ctx.fillStyle  = '#e8eaf6';\n    ctx.font       = 'bold 12px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n    ctx.fillText(box.label || default_header(box), x + 10, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // kind badge (top right)\n    ctx.fillStyle  = color;\n    ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n    ctx.fillText(kind.toUpperCase(), x + w - 8, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // port dots and labels\n    const { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts } = port_positions(box);\n\n    ctx.font      = '10px monospace';\n    ctx.fillStyle = '#9ea3c0';\n\n    in_pts.forEach((p, i) => {\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = '#2d3250';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = '#6c72a0';\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();",

Looking up the index by name keeps callers honest —\n  // they can ask about a port without knowing its row.\n  function port_full_value_if_truncated(box, port_name) {\n    if (!box.inputs) return null;\n    const i = box.inputs.findIndex(p => p.name === port_name);\n    if (i < 0) return null;\n    const p = box.inputs[i];\n    const has_value = p.value !== undefined && p.value !== null && p.value !== '';\n    if (!has_value) return null;\n    if (port_has_incoming_wire(box, p.name)) return null;\n    const raw = String(p.value);\n    return raw === port_label_text(box, i) ? null : raw;\n  }\n  // }}}\n",

    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"who → World\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n    \"input → 5\" \\\n    \"double → 10\" \\\n    \"addone → 11\" \\\n    \"shout → 11!\"\n\npipeline_output_check\ncompile_pipeline_check\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ parser_tests() — issue 232: unit tests for langs/<lang>/parser.js\n# Run Node's built-in test runner over each per-language parser test\n# file and fold the result into the surrounding pass/fail counters.\n# Each .mjs file is one logical \"test\" from this script's perspective;\n# Node prints its own subtest breakdown on failure for the diagnostic.\nparser_tests() {\n    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"  %-44s SKIP — node not installed\\n\" \"parser tests (lua, bash)\"\n        return\n    fi\n    for tf in \"$DIR/tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/234-language-spec-js-test.mjs\"; do\n        local label\n        label=$(basename \"$tf\")\n        printf \"  %-44s \" \"$label\"\n        local out\n        out=$(SORAMECH_DIR=\"$DIR\" node --test \"$tf\" 2>&1)\n        local rc=$?\n        if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL\\n\"\n            echo \"$out\" | sed 's/^/      /'\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"$label: node --test exit=$rc\")\n        fi\n    done\n}\nparser_tests\n# }}}\n\necho\necho \"  $pass passed, $fail failed\"\n\nif [[ $fail -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo\n    echo \"  failures:\"\n    for f in \"${failures[@]}\"; do\n        echo \"    - $f\"\n    done\nfi\n\nexit $fail\n",

          "new_string":"## Implementation log\n\n### 2026-05-19 — phase 3 + editor\n\nWhat landed:\n\n- **Kind rename** in the C runtime. `BOX_DATA` → `BOX_READ`,\n  `BOX_FILE_WRITE` → `BOX_WRITE`. The schema accepts only the new\n  string names; the old `\"data\"` / `\"file_write\"` strings are\n  unrecognised. Per the project's \"no users to migrate\" reality,\n  fixtures were edited by hand rather than building a one-shot\n  loader migration.\n\n- **Inline literal `value` on `read`.** A read box with `\"value\":\n  \"...\"` in its JSON emits those bytes directly — no file IO, no\n  path required. When `value` is unset the read box falls back to\n  the existing file-source path (static `path` field). The\n  \"path arrives via input wire\" case is left as a follow-on\n  slice; today's fixtures all use the static or literal path.\n\n- **Boolean done output on `write`.** Write boxes are no longer\n  silent sinks. After a successful write, the box pushes `\"true\"`\n  through `push_routed` like any other producer. Unwired output\n  is discarded — the existing fan-to-zero-consumers path in\n  `push_to_downstream` is the unwired-output rule made concrete.\n  The pipeline fixture verifies both: the file gets `\"11!\"`, and\n  the runner's outputs section shows `output → true`.\n\n- **Editor surface.**\n    * `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `KIND_COLOR` gains `read: #4caf7d`\n      (green, kept from the legacy data colour) and `write:\n      #d4762a` (warm cheddar, contrasts visibly against read).\n      `KIND_HEADER` gains both kinds. A new `visible_inputs()`\n      helper hides the `path` port on a read box when `value` is\n      set — the layout (height, port positions, hit testing) all\n      route through it, so the port disappears consistently.\n    * `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — kind dropdown is now `['call',\n      'read', 'write']`. A new `render_io_box()` branch attaches\n      a `value` textarea for read boxes (typing into it\n      re-renders so the canvas port-hide toggles immediately) and\n      skips the call-box machinery (ref/fn/routing don't apply).\n    * `src/001-schema.lua` — `valid_kinds` accepts `call` / `read`\n      / `write`. The shape check for read / write is permissive:\n      `value` and `path` must be strings if set, `inputs` an\n      array. Semantic enforcement (\"has a value or a path\")\n      lives in the graph loader.\n\n- **Integration fixture.** `tests/maps/read-literal/` exercises\n  the inline-value path end-to-end: a read box with `\"value\":\n  \"hello, world!\"` feeds a Lua echo box. The new entry in\n  `run-tests.sh` asserts `src → hello, world!` and `echo → hello,\n  world!` appear in the runner output.\n\n### What was deferred and why\n\n**Language-aware IO on cross-language wires.** The design above\ncalls for the dispatch layer to call `source.native_to_json` and\n`target.json_to_native` at every cross-language seam, so a Lua\nbox returning a table reaches a C consumer as a typed struct (or\nvice versa). That cannot happen with today's invoke / slot-store\ncontract: the spec's `invoke` writes bytes to `out_buf`, and the\nbridges from issue 317 use a stack-protocol (read top of\n`lua_State`, push to top). The two contracts don't align — a\nbridge can't read a stack value that the spec already\ndiscarded after writing to `out_buf`.\n\nBridging that gap is a real change with two viable shapes:\n\n1. The slot store grows a \"native handle\" alternative — a slot\n   carries either bytes or a \"look at top of producer's stack\"\n   token, and the consumer's spec is responsible for consuming\n   it.\n2. The invoke chain is restructured so producers leave values on\n   the working store and the dispatcher pulls them via\n   `native_to_json`.\n\nEither is a larger refactor than 229's box-kind work, and\nneither is on the critical path for the current fixtures (every\nexisting cross-language wire is text-shaped today). The deferral\nis documented here and in issue 317's \"Next implementation\nslices\" section.\n\n### Files touched\n\n- `src/010-graph-loader.{h,c}` — kind rename; `value` field on box_t;\n  schema parses `\"read\"` / `\"write\"`; comments updated.\n- `src/012-dispatch.c` — `do_data_box` → `do_read_box` with literal\n  path; `do_file_write_box` → `do_write_box` that pushes `\"true\"`;\n  dispatch action's switch updated; the sink-skip guard removed.\n- `src/010-graph-loader.info.md` — public-surface enum names.\n- `tests/010-graph-loader-test.c` — kind name updated in `who`\n  assertions.\n- `tests/maps/{pipeline,hello}/boxes/*.json` — fixture rename.\n- `tests/maps/pipeline/boxes/shout.json` — connection's `to_input`\n  follows the rename to `value`.\n- `tests/maps/read-literal/` — new fixture exercising the inline\n  literal path.\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh` — read-literal entry + the\n  `pipeline file_write output` label renamed to `pipeline write\n  output`.\n- `src/001-schema.lua`, `assets/js/002-boxes.js`,\n  `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — editor surface per the kind list.\n\n## Historical proposals (superseded)",
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"## Historical proposals (superseded)",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/229-data-box-as-language-agnostic-file-io.md"

Inline literal `value` OR file at `path`.              |\n| `write` | no               | File sink. Writes the `value` input; emits boolean `\"true\"` downstream. |\n\n`read` and `write` are dispatch-layer primitives — the runtime\nreads/writes the file directly, no language spec is invoked. A\n`read` box with an inline `value` literal skips file IO entirely\nand emits the literal bytes. A `write` box atomically commits\nits `value` input to disk and pushes `\"true\"` to any downstream\nwires; if no wire reads its output, the boolean is discarded per\nthe unwired-output rule.\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"from_file\", \"kind\": \"read\", \"path\": \"config.json\",\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 100 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"from_literal\", \"kind\": \"read\",\n  \"value\": \"hello, world!\",\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 200 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"save\", \"kind\": \"write\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"path\",  \"type\": \"string\" },\n    { \"name\": \"value\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 400, \"y\": 100 } }\n```\n\n**Unwired-output discard rule.** If an output value is produced\nbut no wire carries it downstream, the value is discarded. A\n`write` box with no wire on its done-boolean output still\ncommits the file — the boolean just goes nowhere. The rule\napplies to every kind; `write` is the most visible case.",

A\n`read` box with an inline `value` literal skips file IO entirely\nand emits the literal bytes. A `write` box atomically commits\nits `value` input to disk and pushes `\"true\"` to any downstream\nwires; if no wire reads its output, the boolean is discarded per\nthe unwired-output rule.\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"from_file\", \"kind\": \"read\", \"path\": \"config.json\",\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 100 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"from_literal\", \"kind\": \"read\",\n  \"value\": \"hello, world!\",\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 200 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"save\", \"kind\": \"write\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"path\",  \"type\": \"string\" },\n    { \"name\": \"value\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 400, \"y\": 100 } }\n```\n\n**Unwired-output discard rule.** If an output value is produced\nbut no wire carries it downstream, the value is discarded. A\n`write` box with no wire on its done-boolean output still\ncommits the file — the boolean just goes nowhere. The rule\napplies to every kind; `write` is the most visible case.",

    "originalFile":"# 010-graph-loader.c — public surface\n\nC graph loader (phase 3). Reads a map directory, parses every\nJSON file, and produces an in-memory `graph_t` the dispatch layer\nand pool runner consume. Replaces `src/003-loader.lua`.\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- `graph_t *graph_load(const char *map_dir, char **err)` — read +\n  parse + validate. Returns NULL on any failure and sets `*err` to\n  a malloc'd `\"<file>:<line>: <message>\"` diagnostic. The caller\n  frees `*err`.\n- `void graph_destroy(graph_t *g)` — frees every byte the graph\n  owns (the box and connection arrays, the input declarations, the\n  underlying JSON arena holding every string).\n\n## Accessors\n\n- `const char *graph_name(g)`\n- `const char *graph_description(g)`\n- `const char *graph_entry_box_id(g)`\n- `int          graph_n_boxes(g)`\n- `const box_t *graph_box(g, i)`\n- `const box_t *graph_box_by_id(g, id)`\n\n## Public types\n\n- `box_kind_t` — `BOX_CALL` / `BOX_READ` / `BOX_WRITE`.\n- `routing_kind_t` — `ROUTING_PLAIN` / `ROUTING_COMPARATOR` /\n  `ROUTING_ITERATOR`; randomizer / weighted / distributor enum\n  values exist but the parser doesn't accept them yet.\n- `routing_t` — `kind` plus per-kind params (`n_outputs`,\n  `comparand`).\n- `input_decl_t` — `name`, `type`, `literal`, `optional`.\n- `connection_t` — outgoing connection. Stores string refs\n  (`to_box`, `to_input`); resolved-to-integer-index forms come in\n  the topology iteration.\n- `box_t` — all of the above per box.\n\n## Schema currently enforced\n\n- `meta.json` must be a JSON object containing at least `name`.\n- Every file under `boxes/` ending in `.json` is a box file with a\n  top-level object, `id` (string), `kind` ∈ `{call, data, file_write}`.\n- `call` boxes: require `ref` and `routing`. `fn` is optional (a\n  language without function-name dispatch is fine). `lang` is\n  optional too — falls back to inference from `ref` extension once\n  the spec registry lands.\n- `data` boxes: require `path`; no `ref` / `fn` / `routing`.\n- `file_write` boxes: no kind-specific required fields beyond\n  inputs.\n- `routing.kind` ∈ `{plain, comparator, iterator}` (issue 233's\n  shipped surface). `comparator` requires `comparand` (number or\n  string-form number per the issue's example shape).\n  `iterator` requires `n_outputs` (>= 1).\n- Box ids must be unique across the map. O(n²) scan; n is small.\n\n## What's NOT here (deferred to follow-on iterations within 305)\n\n- **Phase 4 — topology validation.** Connection endpoints aren't\n  resolved to integer indices yet; we don't verify that every\n  `to_box` refers to a real box, nor that the `to_input` matches a\n  declared port. Cycle detection (excluding iterator-rooted\n  cycles) lands here too.\n- **Phase 5 — slot size class enumeration.** The slot store's\n  `slot_alloc` consumes a `cell_capacity`; the loader's job is to\n  scan box outputs and enumerate the distinct sizes the graph\n  needs.\n- **Phase 6 — entry-box detection.** Boxes with no inputs (or\n  inputs fed only by `data` boxes) get auto-detected as entry\n  points.\n- **Phase 7 — language enumeration.** Walk every call box,\n  collect distinct `lang` values, hand the set to the spec\n  registry.\n- The remaining routing kinds (`randomizer`, `weighted`,\n  `distributor`) — issue 233 deferred them to their own\n  follow-ons; the parser rejects them with a precise message.\n\nNone of these block issues 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n\n## Related\n\n- Issue 305 — design.\n- Issue 233 — unified routing schema this loader implements.\n- Issue 229 — data / file_write box kinds.\n- Issue 314 — the JSON parser this depends on.\n- Issue 302 — slot store; the loader will eventually hand size\n  class enumeration to it.\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.info.md"
  },

          "command":"git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n229 — read and write box kinds, with the editor surface to match\n\nThe old data / file_write kinds always wore the wrong names. A box\nnamed \"data\" doesn't say what it does; a sink named \"file_write\"\nhides that it's a sink in a noun. Rename to verbs — read and write —\nand reshape both to fit the data they actually move.\n\nA read box now emits a value. Sometimes that value lives in a file\nand you give the box a path; sometimes the value is a small literal\nyou type in the inspector. Setting an inline value hides the path\nport on the canvas — the box that has no file no longer pretends to\nhave one.\n\nA write box no longer disappears the moment it commits to disk. It\nemits the boolean true downstream, so graphs that want to chain on\n\"and now the file exists\" can fire whatever comes next; graphs that\ndon't care drop the boolean per the unwired-output rule. The same\nrule already held informally everywhere; making it visible at the\nsink puts it in writing.\n\nThe editor's kind dropdown, the box colours, the header labels, the\ninspector layout, and the architecture doc all line up behind the\nnew names. One end-to-end fixture exercises the inline-literal\npath. The cross-language slice — where a Lua table reaches a C\nstruct natively across the wire — remains a documented next step,\nbecause the bridges from 317 and the slot store don't yet share a\nshape. Phase 2 was skipped on purpose; its days are numbered.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
